primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage renal disease (CKD stage 5) secondary to diabetic nephropathy
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily; titrate to 5 mg after 2 weeks if tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration step
medications.purpose: Reduce intraglomerular pressure, lower proteinuria and blood pressure; slows CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line_treatment: ACE inhibitor for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction; CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line_treatment: Statin for all CKD patients for cardiovascular risk reduction

medications.dose: 10 units subcutaneously at bedtime; titrate to achieve fasting glucose 4.4–7.2 mmol/L
medications.duration: Indefinite — review glucose logs after 1 week, then monthly
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control; metformin contraindicated at eGFR <30
medications.nice_justification: CKD stage 5 with diabetes: insulin is recommended when oral agents are contraindicated (NG203 guidance on diabetes in CKD)

medications.duration: Add if blood pressure remains >140/90 mmHg after 4 weeks of ACE‑I; review BP in 2 weeks and adjust as needed
medications.purpose: Adjunct antihypertensive to achieve target <140/90 (or <130/80 with ACR ≥70)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 non‑pharmacological: BP target <140/90; CCB safe in advanced CKD
NG203 recommends addressing dyslipidaemia; omega‑3 can be used when TG >200 mg/dL

interactions_checked.action: Do not add potassium‑sparing agents unless serum K⁺ ≤5.0 mmol/L and monitored closely

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased statin plasma levels → myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Avoid concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or switch to pravastatin if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR 10.5 mL/min/1.73m² (<30) – risk of lactic acidosis
Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention in eGFR <30
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol for pain; refer to pain specialist for alternatives

contraindications.reason: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury in advanced CKD
contraindications.alternative: Use either ramipril OR losartan, not both

contraindications.reason: Guideline indication requires eGFR ≥20; patient eGFR 10.5
contraindications.alternative: Not applicable; insulin is preferred for glycaemic control

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure reading not provided – assume above target; amlodipine added only if needed.
Serum potassium and liver function tests not available – baseline labs required before starting ramipril and atorvastatin.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, ARB, statin, or insulin allergies before prescribing.
Patient may be using over‑the‑counter NSAIDs for chronic pain – counsel to stop and use paracetamol instead.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 5 mg) to control BP and proteinuria, initiate atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for CV risk reduction, begin insulin glargine 10 U at bedtime for diabetes management (metformin contraindicated), add amlodipine 5 mg daily only if BP remains uncontrolled, and consider omega‑3 1 g twice daily for triglyceride control. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, lipids, and glucose per NICE NG203 recommendations, and avoid NSAIDs, metformin, and ACE‑I/ARB combination.
